value.body: A B.Com with a finance focus — named B.Com (Finance), B.Com (Accounting & Finance) or B.Com (Financial Markets) at some universities, and a set of electives at others. You study financial management, investment analysis, financial markets and institutions, and corporate finance, on top of core accounting, economics, statistics and business law.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 (commerce preferred, not always required). Central and many other universities admit through CUET-UG; others admit on Class 12 marks or their own process. Some finance-heavy Honours courses expect Mathematics in Class 12. Where finance is a named programme you choose it at admission; elsewhere you pick finance electives.

value.title: At a glance
items: Several market-facing roles need SEBI-mandated NISM certifications — for example to distribute mutual funds or register as a research analyst.
Entry roles are often in operations, credit, research support or client servicing at banks, brokerages, fund houses and finance back-offices.
Spreadsheet and financial-modelling skills are commonly tested in hiring.
Common add-ons: CFA, FRM, CA or CMA, or an MBA (Finance).
